Egypt adopted a responsible-AI charter stating that government AI projects should undergo impact assessment, be supervised by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, and generate periodic reports for the National AI Council, with annual review of the charter; however, the source does not show implementation, auditing, or enforcement (BATCH-0020-E001; BATCH-0020-E002). The operative surveillance framework allowed security agencies access to retained user data without judicial orders, exempted national-security authorities from data-protection obligations, did not guarantee an independent data-protection regulator, and remained incompletely implemented because executive regulations were absent (BATCH-0002-E041; BATCH-0009-R01-E011; BATCH-0009-R02-E018; BATCH-0009-R02-E019). During 2023, reporting described opaque surveillance and monitoring without consistent judicial-warrant support, including high-confidence technical attribution of Predator spyware targeting opposition candidate Ahmed Tantawy to the Egyptian government; this attribution does not establish Sisi’s personal authorization or a judicial finding (BATCH-0002-E012; BATCH-0002-E040; BATCH-0009-R03-E005). Authorities also used legal and administrative mechanisms to block or investigate independent websites, including a six-month Mada Masr blocking, while the stated licensing and false-news grounds were disputed or accompanied by the outlet’s response (BATCH-0002-E035; BATCH-0009-R03-E007). Separately, security forces arrested more than 2,000 people for peaceful expression or assembly from early 2023 through mid-September, and surveillance and repression of online critics were reported (BATCH-0002-E007; BATCH-0002-E012). The COP27-app allegations concern November 2022 rather than the target year and were disputed by an Egyptian official, so they provide inherited context rather than direct 2023 proof (BATCH-0009-R01-E010; personal presidential involvement is not shown."],"corrections_made":["Separated direct 2023 evidence from inherited legal and 2022 COP27-app context.","Added the absence of an independent data-protection regulator and the suspended data-protection safeguards.","Replaced the unsupported composite claim of administrative harassment with specifically documented arrests, surveillance, investigations, and website blocking.","Preserved the favorable AI-governance measure while limiting it to formal policy design without demonstrated enforcement.","Clarified technical spyware attribution, disputed allegations, and the absence of proof of personal presidential authorization."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["New evidence could clarify procurement, authorization, oversight, or presidential knowledge concerning surveillance and spyware.","The assessment could change if implementation and enforcement of the responsible-AI charter or data-protection framework are documented.","A fuller 2023 record of shutdowns, takedown orders, and regulator decisions could better establish the breadth and ruler attribution of digital controls."]}
